evals.prompt: Select the right directory integration for three WorkSpaces deployments: (A) 300 Windows developers needing GPOs, two-way forest trust with on-prem AD, and native FSx for Windows File Server mounts; (B) 150 finance users authenticating directly against existing on-prem domain controllers over Direct Connect without deploying cloud DCs; and (C) 400 cloud-first SaaS shift workers on WorkSpaces Pools + Entra ID-joined Personal desktops with zero AD domain controllers.
evals.expected_output: Maps all three cleanly: (A) **AWS Managed Microsoft AD** — native AWS-managed domain controllers supporting GPOs, forest trusts with on-prem AD, and seamless FSx for Windows File Server integration; (B) **AD Connector** — stateless directory proxy forwarding DNS/LDAPS/Kerberos authentication over low-latency Direct Connect / VPN to existing on-prem AD without cloud DCs; and (C) **AWS IAM Identity Center (SAML 2.0) + Microsoft Entra ID join** — cloud-native identity for WorkSpaces Pools and Entra ID-joined WorkSpaces Personal without managing Active Directory infrastructure.
expectations: Activates the amazon-workspaces-administration skill
Maps (A) to AWS Managed Microsoft AD (GPOs + trusts + FSx Windows) and (B) to AD Connector over Direct Connect (low-latency DNS/LDAPS/Kerberos proxy)
Maps (C) to IAM Identity Center (SAML 2.0 for WorkSpaces Pools) and Entra ID-joined WorkSpaces Personal with zero domain controllers

Applies the ~80 hours/month break-even threshold to assign `AlwaysOn` (`165` hrs/mo) and `AutoStop` with `RunningModeAutoStopTimeoutInMinutes` (`25` hrs/mo)

evals.prompt: Why should our new enterprise WorkSpaces fleet standardize on **WSP (WorkSpaces Streaming Protocol)** instead of legacy PCoIP, and how must we configure storage encryption and KMS key permissions at provisioning time?
evals.expected_output: Explains why **WSP** is mandatory for modern fleets (adaptive UDP/TCP transport over port `4195`, built-in bi-directional audio/video webcam optimization, USB peripheral & smart-card CAC/PIV redirection, and multi-monitor/4K support), and enforces enabling **both `RootVolumeEncryptionEnabled=true` and `UserVolumeEncryptionEnabled=true`** at creation time (cannot be toggled in-place without rebuild/recreate) using a **customer-managed KMS key (CMK)** whose key policy grants `kms:CreateGrant`, `kms:Encrypt`, `kms:Decrypt`, and `kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext` to `workspaces.amazonaws.com`.
expectations: Activates the amazon-workspaces-administration skill
Highlights WSP advantages (adaptive UDP/TCP streaming, bi-directional audio/webcam, USB & smart-card redirection)
Requires `RootVolumeEncryptionEnabled=true` and `UserVolumeEncryptionEnabled=true` with a KMS CMK granting `CreateGrant` and `GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext` to `workspaces.amazonaws.com`

evals.prompt: We have 600 contact-center agents working three 8-hour shifts (max 200 concurrent) who only use a softphone and CRM app, plus 50 CAD engineers needing persistent local `D:\` storage and GPU bundles. Should both groups get WorkSpaces Personal?
evals.expected_output: Splits the architecture across both offerings: (1) **WorkSpaces Pools** for the 600 shift-based contact-center agents — non-persistent pooled virtual desktops sized to **200 concurrent sessions** (instead of paying for 600 persistent desktops!), paired with **FSLogix profile containers** stored on Multi-AZ **Amazon FSx for Windows File Server** so user settings roam across ephemeral sessions; and (2) **WorkSpaces Personal** (`Graphics.g4dn` / GPU WSP bundle, `AlwaysOn` or `AutoStop`) for the 50 CAD engineers requiring dedicated persistent `D:\` user volumes and GPU acceleration.
expectations: Activates the amazon-workspaces-administration skill
Assigns WorkSpaces Pools (sized for ~200 concurrent shift users rather than 600 named desktops) with FSLogix profile containers on Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
Assigns persistent GPU-backed WorkSpaces Personal (`D:\` user volume) for the 50 CAD engineers

evals.prompt: Architect a multi-region disaster recovery design for our primary `us-east-1` WorkSpaces Personal fleet (`us-west-2` DR) so users connect via a single DNS endpoint without re-entering registration codes during a regional outage and keep their user profiles.
evals.expected_output: Designs the complete Multi-Region Resilience pattern: (1) provision **Multi-Region Resilience (Standby WorkSpaces)** in `us-west-2` linked to the primary `us-east-1` WorkSpaces (maintaining replicated root image configuration at low standby cost until promoted); (2) configure **Amazon Route 53 DNS failover** (health-checked primary/secondary records on a custom connection FQDN redirecting to regional registration codes so end users never manually retype registration codes); and (3) store roaming profiles / **FSLogix containers on Amazon FSx for Windows File Server** replicated to `us-west-2` via **AWS Backup cross-region copy** (or NetApp SnapMirror / DFS-R).
expectations: Activates the amazon-workspaces-administration skill
Configures Standby WorkSpaces (Multi-Region Resilience) in `us-west-2` paired with Route 53 DNS failover so users do not manually change registration codes
Persists and replicates user profile containers (FSLogix on FSx for Windows File Server with cross-region AWS Backup copy)

evals.prompt: We updated our Windows 11 WorkSpaces golden image with security patches and created a new custom bundle. Compare `RebootWorkspaces`, `RebuildWorkspaces`, and `MigrateWorkspace` — which operation updates the OS image to the new bundle cleanly, and what happens to files saved on `D:\` 2 hours ago if an admin runs `RebuildWorkspaces`?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes all three operations and flags the data-loss trap: (1) **`RebootWorkspaces`** only restarts the guest OS — it does **not** apply a new image or bundle; (2) **`RebuildWorkspaces`** replaces `C:\` from the current bundle's image AND restores `D:\` **only from the last automatic 12-hour snapshot**, meaning **any `D:\` files created in the last 2 hours (since the snapshot) are permanently lost!**; and (3) **`MigrateWorkspace`** transitions a WorkSpace to the **new target bundle/image**, recreating `C:\` from the new bundle while taking a fresh migration snapshot/copy of `D:\` user profile data (still advise backing up critical user files to FSx/OneDrive before maintenance).
expectations: Activates the amazon-workspaces-administration skill

Contrasts `RebootWorkspaces` (OS restart only), `RebuildWorkspaces` (same bundle reset restoring `D:\` from the last 12-hour snapshot — losing the last 2 hours of unsnapshotted `D:\` changes), and `MigrateWorkspace` (switches to the new custom bundle)
Recommends `MigrateWorkspace` (alongside backing up critical `D:\` user files to FSx / folder redirection / OneDrive before maintenance) for rolling out the new custom bundle

Configures `AWS::WorkSpaces::Workspace` with `RootVolumeEncryptionEnabled: true`, `UserVolumeEncryptionEnabled: true`, KMS key parameter, `RunningMode: AUTO_STOP`, and `RunningModeAutoStopTimeoutInMinutes: 60`
Configures IP access control (`198.51.100.0/24`) using valid CloudFormation/WorkSpaces directory access-control configuration verified against `awsiac`

evals.prompt: Verify against AWS WorkSpaces documentation via MCP: (1) what infrastructure, Microsoft licensing, and minimum commitment/host requirements apply to **Windows 10/11 Bring Your Own License (BYOL)** on Amazon WorkSpaces, and (2) when should an enterprise choose **Amazon WorkSpaces Core** instead of WorkSpaces Personal?

expectations: Activates the amazon-workspaces-administration skill and consults `awsknowledge` / `aws-mcp` documentation tools with zero raw `aws` CLI commands
Explains Windows 10/11 BYOL requirements (single-tenant Dedicated hardware, eligible Microsoft licensing, VM import + AWS Support BYOL onboarding)
